To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the RARE estimator is a simple search-free algorithm that can be used for DOA estimation in the partly calibrated sensor arrays; (ii) its performance in the case of time-varying sensor array can be accurately predicted using the CRBs derived in this thesis; and (iii) the performance of the RARE algorithm in the case of fully calibrated array is the same as the performance of the well-known root-MUSIC algorithm.

the proposed RARE algorithms are capable of achieving near-CRB performance and that DOA estimation in time-varying sensor arrays can be much more accurate than in the corresponding time-invariant array cases.

the RARE algorithm is a computationally simple search-free DOA estimator for partly calibrated and time varying sensor arrays and that the derived CRBs provide an accurate characterization of the finite-sample performance for the RARE algorithms in this class of arrays.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of search-free direction-finding algorithms that are computationally simple and have performance close to the corresponding Cramer-Rao lower bounds for partly calibrated and time-invariant as well as for time-varying sensor arrays.
a new class of sensor arrays that can be considered as a special case of the more general time-varying and nonuniformly spaced sensor arrays.

the development of new search-free algorithms for direction-of-arrival estimation and the derivation of closed-form expressions for the corresponding CRBs in partly calibrated and nonidentical sensor arrays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the proposed algorithms is close to the CRBs, and that the derived CRBs are useful for assessing the performance of the RARE algorithms in this class of sensor arrays.
RARE algorithms are capable of achieving the Cramer-Rao lower bound on DOA estimation for the class of partly calibrated arrays.

the proposed RARE algorithms are capable of achieving the CRB in both the time-invariant and the time-varying cases, and the derived CRBs provide a useful benchmark for the performance evaluation of DOA estimation algorithms for the considered class sensor arrays.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RARE estimators are computationally efficient, simple to implement, robust to calibration errors, and have performance that is close to the theoretical bounds.
the RARE approach is a powerful tool for DOA estimation in the considered class of partly calibrated arrays.
, in the considered class of partly calibrated and time-invariant arrays, the RARE algorithm is a computationally simple and efficient alternative to the conventional MUSIC algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the performance degradation in partly calibrated arrays can be mitigated by using multiple subarrays, and the performance of the proposed RARE estimator is not sensitive to the array calibration errors.
the proposed RARE algorithms can be used to effectively estimate the DOAs of the incident signals in the presence of unknown and time-varyng sensor array displacements.

in the case of partly calibrated and/or time-varying sensor arrays, the performance of DOA estimation is not degraded by the presence of the array displacement, but rather by the array noncalibration.
